title: How does the Merger and Acquisition’s Goodwill Response to the Short-Selling Scheme in China
summary: This study examines how China's short-selling scheme affects goodwill recognized in mergers and acquisitions. Using the short-selling pilot program as a quasi-natural experiment, we employ a staggered difference-in-differences (DID) model based on Chinese A-share listed companies from 2007 to 2020. The results show that the introduction of short selling significantly reduces both the carrying value of goodwill and newly recognized goodwill arising from M&A transactions. These findings remain robust after a series of robustness tests, including parallel trend analysis, entropy balancing matching, and alternative measures of short-selling intensity and goodwill. Further analyses reveal that the governance effect of short selling is more pronounced in firms with severe agency conflicts, weaker regulatory environments, and lower disclosure pressure regarding goodwill-related critical audit matters. The evidence suggests that short selling functions as an effective external governance mechanism by constraining managerial opportunism in acquisition decisions and goodwill accounting, thereby improving the quality of goodwill fair value estimates. This study extends the literature on short selling and goodwill by providing new evidence that market-based governance can mitigate M&A goodwill overvaluation and enhance its quality. The findings also offer important policy implications for regulators seeking to strengthen capital market governance and enhance company’s M&A quality to facilitate investors’ decision-making.

title: Asymmetry in Compensation Peer Group Selection: Reciprocity and Upward Tilt in Disclosed Benchmarking Networks
summary: Compensation committees benchmark pay against a self-selected group of peer companies, and disclose that group. Treating those disclosures as a directed graph, we ask three questions: how reciprocal is peer selection, is it symmetric in firm size, and is asymmetry associated with shareholder support for pay? Using named-peer disclosures from 1,193 active U.S. public companies across twelve industries, of which 993 (83.2%) disclose a placeable peer group, we construct a network of 33,766 peer namings spanning 3,464 distinct companies. Selection is substantially non-mutual: 32.6% of namings are reciprocated, leaving roughly two thirds of peer relationships one-directional. Naming is also concentrated — the most-named firm appears on 65 peer lists — and concentration is stable across a full added proxy season, during which namings grew thirteen percent against a universe that grew less than one percent. The central finding is a persistent upward tilt. The median firm names a peer set approximately twenty percent larger than itself by market capitalisation (aspirational index 1.191, unchanged to three decimals over one season), the ninetieth-percentile firm names peers 3.209 times its own size, and 352 firms name peers at least 1.5 times their size. Nineteen firms exceed a factor of ten, eighteen of them benchmarking within their own industry, a pattern more consistent with repricing than with the absence of comparable firms. Eighteen firms form a stable core present across all four fiscal years, with median reciprocity of 0.765 against 0.394 for the population. Among 979 firms with both a peer group and a say-on-pay record, 26 occupy a high-asymmetry, low-support quadrant. We report these associations without asserting causation: peer selection, firm size and shareholder support are jointly determined, and disclosed groups reflect committee choices we do not observe. **Keywords:** compensation peer groups; benchmarking; reciprocity; network analysis; say-on-pay; corporate governance **JEL:** G34, J33, M52, M12 --- Working paper prepared for the SSRN Corporate Governance Network. title: Pengaruh Good Corporate Governance dan Leverage terhadap Kinerja Keuangan pada Perusahaan Agribisnis yang Terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia Periode 2020–2024
summary: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui pengaruh Good Corporate Governance yang diproksikan dengan Dewan Komisaris Independen dan Ukuran Dewan Direksi serta Leverage yang diproksikan dengan Debt to Equity Ratio terhadap kinerja keuangan yang diukur menggunakan Return on Assets. Sampel yang digunakan dalam penelitian ini adalah perusahaan agribisnis yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia periode 2020–2024. Teknik pengambilan sampel dilakukan menggunakan metode purposive sampling. Total sebanyak 7 perusahaan yang ditentukan sebagai sampel. Metode analisis yang digunakan dalam penelitian ini adalah regresi data panel dengan model Fixed Effect Model menggunakan aplikasi EViews 13. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa secara parsial Dewan Komisaris Independen dan Ukuran Dewan Direksi tidak berpengaruh terhadap kinerja keuangan yang diukur dengan Return on Assets. Sementara itu, Leverage yang diproksikan dengan Debt to Equity Ratio berpengaruh negatif terhadap kinerja keuangan yang diukur dengan Return on Assets. Secara simultan, Dewan Komisaris Independen, Ukuran Dewan Direksi, dan Leverage yang diproksikan dengan Debt to Equity Ratio berpengaruh terhadap kinerja keuangan perusahaan agribisnis yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia periode 2020–2024. summary: The increase of financial technology (fintech) has transfigured the investment setting, offering retail investors state-of-the-art tools to augment their monetary practices. title: Achieving green competitive advantage through environmental CSR: the serial roles of ambidextrous innovation and environmental performance
summary: Purpose This paper highlights how environmental corporate social responsibility (ECSR) leads to green competitive advantage in emerging market manufacturing SMEs by clarifying the capability-building process through which ECSR initiatives add value under institutional restrictions. Design/methodology/approach This paper draws on the Natural Resource-Based View and ambidexterity theory to develop and test a serial mediation model whereby ECSR leads to green ambidextrous innovation that results in enhanced environmental performance and, ultimately, improved green competitive advantage. A sample of 385 managers from manufacturing SMEs in Jordan was surveyed, and the data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4. Findings Our findings show a significant sequential pathway where ECSR leads to green ambidextrous innovation, which in turn improves environmental performance and leads to green competitive advantage. ECSR also has direct effects. Green ambidextrous innovation and environmental performance play a key role in converting ECSR to competitive advantage. Practical implications Managers must integrate ECSR as a dynamic ability and strive to develop ambidextrous green innovation, balancing incremental enhancements and radical eco-innovations. It is recommended that policymakers put in place enabling regulatory and financial policies to support green resource transitions in resource-constrained industrial sectors. Originality/value Using evidence from Jordan's manufacturing SMEs, this study advances the CSR–performance literature by providing a process-based explanation of how ECSR translates into competitive outcomes. By identifying a sequential capability-building pathway linking ECSR, green ambidextrous innovation and environmental performance, the study clarifies how sustainability advantages emerge over time in resource-constrained and institutionally constrained contexts.

title: Analyzing the Impact of Digital Payment Adoption (UPI/FinTech) on Rural Retailers and Agro-Traders
summary: Digital payment adoption has become an important component of India’s financial and commercial transformation, with Unified Payments Interface (UPI), mobile banking, QR-code payments and other FinTech-enabled services increasingly connecting small businesses with customers and formal financial institutions. This paper examines the impact of digital payment adoption on rural retailers and agro-traders, who operate in environments characterized by cash dependence, seasonal demand, informal credit, dispersed customers, variable connectivity and limited access to formal financial services. The study uses a secondary research approach by synthesizing academic literature, institutional reports and information published by payment-system stakeholders. The analysis focuses on the effects of digital payments on transaction convenience, payment speed, record-keeping, transparency, customer reach, working-capital visibility, financial inclusion and the potential for formal credit access. It also identifies constraints such as poor network connectivity, digital literacy gaps, cyber-fraud concerns, trust issues, device limitations, transaction failures and the continued preference for cash. Recent evidence shows that UPI has reached very large transaction volumes nationally, while research on small merchants indicates that adoption is shaped not only by infrastructure but also by perceived customer demand, expected benefits and concerns around formalization. For rural retailers and agro-traders, digital payments therefore represent not simply a payment method but a business capability that can strengthen transaction efficiency and financial visibility when supported by reliable infrastructure, training and consumer adoption. The paper concludes that a balanced strategy combining digital literacy, dependable connectivity, merchant support, grievance redressal, cyber-security awareness and financial inclusion measures is necessary for sustainable digital payment adoption in rural markets.

title: Étude des applications des technologies de l'industrie alimentaire 4.0 pour la traçabilité et la durabilité des chaînes logistiques agroalimentaire : cas de la filière halio-industrielle
summary: Résumé Cet article propose une mutualisation des technologies émergentes de l’industrie 4.0 comme la technologie de blockchain, Internet des objets et d'intelligence artificielle afin d’aboutir à une chaîne logistique durable, performante et transparente. Toutefois la plupart des recherches restreint leur analyse sur l’apport spécifique de l’une de ces technologies au lieu d’avoir une vision intégrée de l’usage combiné de ces technologies ce qui entrave la transition digitale de la chaîne logistique. Pour combler cette lacune, on a commencé par une analyse de la revue de la littérature systématique qui identifie les technologies émergentes les plus citées et examine leur contribution durable dans la chaîne logistique de l’industrie alimentaire. Par ailleurs, nous avons mené une étude exploratoire dans le domaine halio-industriel pour identifier l’usage de ces technologies au Maroc et au niveau international, en offrant un aperçu détaillé des fonctionnalités et avantage de leur adoption pour assurer une meilleure transparence et durabilité de la chaîne logistique. Les résultats de ces deux études mettent en évidence le potentiel des technologies émergentes de l’industrie 4.0 pour répondre aux préoccupations durables de la chaîne logistique et soulèvent le défi de la mutualisation de ces technologies pour réussir la transition digitale et durable. Mots clés : industrie alimentaire 4.0, blockchain, internet des objets, intelligence artificielle, chaîne logistique halio-industrielle, transition digitale durable Abstract This article proposes a pooling of emerging Industry 4.0 technologies, such as blockchain, the Internet of Things, and artificial intelligence, to achieve a sustainable, efficient, and transparent supply chain. However, most research focuses its analysis on the specific contribution of one of these technologies instead of taking an integrated view of their combined use, thus hindering the digital transformation of the supply chain. To address this gap, we began with a systematic literature review that identifies the most frequently cited emerging technologies and examines their sustainable contribution to the food industry supply chain. Furthermore, we conducted an exploratory study in the seafood industry to identify the use of these technologies in Morocco and internationally, providing a detailed overview of the functionalities and advantages of their adoption to ensure greater transparency and sustainability of the supply chain. The results of these two studies highlight the potential of emerging Industry 4.0 technologies to address the sustainability concerns of the supply chain and raise the challenge of pooling these technologies to successfully achieve the digital and sustainable transition. Keywords : Food industry 4.0, blockchain, internet of things, artificial intelligence, halio-industrial supply chain, sustainable digital transition

title: Earnings Manipulation in State-Owned Enterprises: How Financial Constraints Shape Firms’ Behavior
summary: This study examines how varying levels of state-controlled ownership are associated with earnings management among Indian state-owned enterprises (SOEs) during the period 2005–2022. We further explore the role of financial constraints in moderating the relationship between state ownership and earnings management. Using panel regression, we find a nonlinear U-shaped relationship between state ownership and earnings management, with a threshold level at 67%, beyond which the sensitivity of earnings management to state ownership becomes positive. Our analysis suggests that beyond this threshold point, earnings manipulation in SOEs becomes vigorous with absolute control over the firm. Moreover, under high financial constraints, this U-shape flattens due to the soft budget constraints. Firms anticipating government support face weaker incentives to manipulate earnings due to assured financing. However, profitability becomes more responsive to changes in the level of state ownership under high financial constraints. We validate our findings using alternative estimation techniques and alternative measures of earnings management. Our further analysis reveals that larger board size and increased board independence reduce the opportunistic behavior of state-ownership. Our findings offer implications for strategic disinvestment decisions in SOEs and provide investors with informative signals regarding governance quality.

title: Privacy-Aware Data-Model Dual-Driven Decision Analysis for Data Security in Distributed Multi-Agent Operations
summary: INTRODUCTION: Distributed networks generate heterogeneous security telemetry while moving data across endpoints, users, services, and operational domains. SOCs need methods that protect data assets, preserve auditability, and avoid unsafe tool calls.OBJECTIVES: This paper proposes a data-model dual-driven method, in which incident and execution data constrain LLM-based reasoning while model outputs generate auditable process data, for privacy-aware data security decision analysis in multi-agent security operations.METHODS: The method combines LLM-based role agents, SOAR playbook orchestration, persistent message state, and a virtual security capability layer. Incidents are transformed into data-aware tasks, actions, commands, execution records, and summaries.RESULTS: On 83 labeled incident samples, tool-call evaluation achieved 0.9684 precision, 0.4742 recall, 0.6367 F1-score, and 76.45 s average handling time.CONCLUSION: The method supports auditable data security monitoring and controlled response, while complex multi-step planning remains the main improvement target.

title: Hedging in uncertainty: a quantile coherency approach to Islamic, ESG, and conventional stock resilience
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine the dynamic relationship between conventional, Islamic and ESG stock returns, and various financial, non-financial and policy-related uncertainties. Additionally, the study examines the hedging potential and interconnectedness of these indices under varying market conditions. Design/methodology/approach The study uses a novel method of quantile coherency, introduced by Baruník and Kley (2019), which facilitates in-depth analysis of the dependence structure across quantiles and frequencies. It enables the identification of co-movement patterns among stock returns and uncertainty measures in both standard and extreme market conditions. Additionally, this study uses impulse response functions and dynamic conditional correlation (DCC)-GJR-GARCH approaches for robustness. Findings The results indicate a positive connection between the returns of these stock indices and non-financial uncertainty, particularly in the extreme low and high quantiles over yearly periods, highlighting the effective hedging capability of different stock indices against geopolitical risks. Regarding policy-related uncertainty, the authors observe a significant positive correlation between these stock indices and economic policy uncertainty, particularly at the monthly frequency during bearish market conditions. Furthermore, most conventional, Islamic and ESG stock returns exhibit a negative correlation with financial uncertainties, indicating a lack of effectiveness in hedging against crude oil volatility and implied stock volatility. The robustness of these findings is checked by time-varying correlation (DCC-GJR-GARCH) analysis. Originality/value The results have significant implications for investors, portfolio managers, and policymakers, particularly those seeking to construct a portfolio suitable for all market conditions. This study is among the first to apply quantile coherency analysis to explore how Islamic, ESG and conventional stock markets respond to a broad spectrum of uncertainties.

title: Embedding ESG in SMEs : The Roles of Social Capital, Organisational Learning and Environmental Dynamism
summary: ABSTRACT Although environmental, social and governance (ESG) has become a defining benchmark for corporate sustainability, many small and medium‐sized enterprises (SMEs) continue to struggle to develop and embed effective ESG strategies because of resource constraints. Advancing ESG strategy requires more than tangible assets; it depends on how SMEs leverage network relationships and transform external knowledge into organisational learning capabilities. Drawing upon Social Capital Theory, the Knowledge‐Based View and Institutional Theory, this study develops and tests an integrated framework explaining how SMEs leverage network relationships to develop ESG strategies through organisational learning and ultimately improve competitive advantage. Using a two‐wave, time‐lagged survey of 200 Malaysian SMEs and partial least squares path modelling, the findings show that social capital significantly enhances organisational learning, which mediates its effect on ESG strategy, while environmental dynamism strengthens the relationship between organisational learning and ESG strategy. ESG strategy subsequently strengthens competitive advantage. An importance–performance map analysis further reveals that ESG strategy is the most influential driver of competitive advantage but remains underperforming, indicating considerable unrealised strategic potential. Environmental dynamism also emerged as an influential contextual factor, highlighting the importance of developing adaptive capabilities and strategic agility to respond effectively to increasingly dynamic business environments. The study advances ESG scholarship by integrating Social Capital Theory, the Knowledge‐Based View and Institutional Theory into a capability‐building framework and offers practical guidance for SMEs seeking to develop and embed effective ESG strategies to enhance long‐term competitiveness.

title: ESG as a Catalyst for Sustainable Growth: Insight from Leading Indian Automobile Companies
summary: This study examines Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance as a strategic tool for long-term growth in selected Indian automobile companies. Using a sample of ten Nifty Auto Index companies over five financial years (2020-21 to 2024-25), the study analyzes the relationship between ESG disclosure scores and key financial performance metrics: Return on Equity (ROE), Return on Assets (ROA), and Net Assets. The methodology employs a content analysis approach, wherein ESG disclosures from annual reports and sustainability reports were systematically examined using a structured checklist of 68 ESG indicators derived from BRSR and GRI frameworks to identify and score the extent of ESG performance reporting by each company. Judgmental (non-probability) sampling was applied to select the ten companies. Statistical techniques including Descriptive Statistics, Pearson Correlation Analysis, and Regression Analysis were subsequently applied to assess ESG-financial performance linkages. Results reveal that the average ESG score improved from 0.829 to 0.951, while mean ROE grew from 0.064 to 0.198 and ROA from 0.051 to 0.095 over the study period. Pearson correlation analysis shows moderate positive correlations between ESG scores and both ROE (r = 0.43) and ROA (r = 0.34). Multiple regression confirms that ESG has an independent positive effect on ROE even after controlling for asset efficiency, with the model explaining approximately 39% of ROE variance. The findings conclude that strong ESG practices contribute to long-term corporate sustainability and improved firm performance in the Indian automobile sector, establishing ESG as a genuine strategic management tool rather than a mere regulatory obligation.

title: What Scientific Evidence Identifies An Audit of the Move from Representation to Ontological Commitment
summary: Scientific models can be highly successful while leaving open what, exactly, their formal structures warrant us in claiming about reality. This paper develops a methodological audit for examining the move from successful representation to ontological commitment. The central proposal is not a new criterion of reality or a new identifiability theorem. Instead, the paper separates several inferential questions that are often compressed into a single claim of confirmation: formal identifiability, physical reference, ontological status, fundamentality, and adequacy of the candidate space. Within ontological status, it further distinguishes existential, categorical, and realization claims. Three elementary diagnostics are used to locate where additional warrant must enter an ontological argument: evidence cannot provide likelihood-based discrimination between contrasts to which it is conditionally insensitive; deterministic post-processing cannot create discrimination absent from its complete evidential input; and uniqueness within a specified model class does not by itself establish unrestricted ontological uniqueness. A worked audit of intervention-based causal representation learning demonstrates the method on a technically substantive case. It shows how interventions can genuinely reduce representational freedom and support strong class-relative structural identification while leaving further questions of physical reference, realization, and fundamentality dependent on additional evidence or independently warranted premises. The broader aim is evidential accounting rather than metaphysical prescription: ontological conclusions should be stated at the strongest level for which the relevant contrast has actually been discriminated.

title: Pengaruh Good Corporate Governance, Investment Opportunity Set, Konservatisme Akuntansi terhadap Kualitas Laba (Perusahaan Sektor Consumer Non-Cyclicals yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia periode 2020-2024)
summary: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh good corporate governance, investment opportunity set, dan konservatisme akuntansi terhadap kualitas laba pada perusahaan sektor consumer non-cyclicals yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia periode 2020–2024. Kualitas laba menjadi salah satu aspek penting dalam menilai kemampuan perusahaan menghasilkan informasi laba yang dapat mencerminkan kondisi ekonomi perusahaan secara andal. Penerapan good corporate governance, keberadaan peluang investasi, serta kebijakan konservatisme akuntansi dipandang dapat memengaruhi kualitas informasi laba yang disajikan perusahaan. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode kuantitatif dengan pendekatan asosiatif. Penentuan sampel dilakukan menggunakan teknik purposive sampling berdasarkan kriteria yang telah ditetapkan. Data penelitian bersumber dari laporan tahunan dan laporan keuangan perusahaan sektor consumer non-cyclicals yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia selama periode penelitian. Analisis data dilakukan menggunakan regresi data panel dengan bantuan aplikasi EViews 13. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa secara simultan good corporate governance, investment opportunity set, dan konservatisme akuntansi berpengaruh terhadap kualitas laba. Hal tersebut menunjukkan bahwa ketiga variabel tersebut secara bersama-sama memiliki kemampuan dalam menjelaskan perubahan kualitas laba perusahaan, sehingga hipotesis pertama diterima. Secara parsial, good corporate governance tidak berpengaruh terhadap kualitas laba. Investment opportunity set juga tidak berpengaruh terhadap kualitas laba. Sementara itu, konservatisme akuntansi berpengaruh terhadap kualitas laba. Temuan tersebut menunjukkan bahwa penerapan kebijakan akuntansi yang konservatif memiliki peran dalam menentukan kualitas laba yang dihasilkan perusahaan, sedangkan good corporate governance dan investment opportunity set belum menunjukkan pengaruh secara individual terhadap kualitas laba pada perusahaan sektor consumer non-cyclicals selama periode 2020–2024.

title: The creation of SDG auditing as a proto-institution: the role of institutional work
summary: Purpose The aim of this study is to explore what types of institutional work (IW) an actor of change, the INTOSAI Development Initiative (IDI), used to create sustainable development goals (SDGs) auditing practices for supreme audit institutions (SAIs). Design/methodology/approach Building on IW and theoretical concepts of proto-institutions, we examine the case of IDI promoting the diffusion of SDG auditing practices throughout national SAIs worldwide. The paper draws on longitudinal data (secondary and primary sources, respectively, official IDI sources and interviews with IDI professionals working with SDG audits) collected between 2021 and 2025, reflecting key stages in the development of SDG auditing. Findings Our findings suggest that the creation of SDG auditing as a proto-institution is best understood as a contested process of institutional adaptation. The creation of SDG auditing was not intended to replace existing practices but rather to reinforce them to meet the current challenges defined by the UN's 2030 Agenda. We observe that SDG audits appear to repurpose existing performance audits with new concepts and principles linked to the 2030 Agenda and can be seen as gradual change mechanisms that ensure the continued existence and relevance of institutions. The diverse IW strategies were motivated by the objective of creating SDG auditing as an augmentation of performance auditing. The findings demonstrate that SDG auditing emerged as a proto-institution rather than as a new institution in the traditional sense. Originality/value This paper presents a case of the creation of an institution (i.e. SDG auditing) through interactions between IDI and multiple actors, aimed at reinforcing and repurposing existing public auditing practices such as performance audits. We offer a nuanced view on how the IW of a proto-institution creation is part of an overall strategy by a change agent (IDI) to develop an established institutional field (i.e. performance audits) by gaining legitimacy, support and engaging stakeholders. The proto-institution of SDG audits thus represents an augmentation or adaptation of an existing practice for new purposes, consistent with the view of institutions as “multipurpose tools”.

title: GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN VOCATIONAL UNDERGRADUATE FINANCE AND ACCOUNTING EDUCATION: APPLICATIONS, RISKS, AND FUTURE DIRECTIONS
summary: Generative artificial intelligence is entering finance and accounting classrooms before curricula, assessment systems, and institutional controls have fully adapted. This narrative review explains the technical principles of large language models and examines their use in vocational undergraduate finance and accounting education. Potential applications include dialogic tutoring, formative feedback, text simplification, case simulation, spreadsheet and programming support, financial analysis, professional communication, and course design. These functions can make practice more accessible and provide rapid opportunities for comparison and revision. Their educational value, however, depends on how the task is structured. Fluent output may contain fabricated facts, obsolete rules, incorrect calculations, biased assumptions, or unsupported recommendations. Unrestricted assistance may also improve immediate task performance without developing the independent knowledge and professional judgment that students need. Additional concerns include academic misconduct, confidential-data exposure, unequal access, unreliable detection, and weak accountability. A responsible integration model should therefore separate AI-free foundations, guided AI assistance, and AI-critical professional tasks. It should require authoritative-source verification, calculation checks, process records, disclosure, reflection, and oral or practical defense. Future systems may combine domain-controlled retrieval, multimodal simulations, and auditable learning records, but vocational programmes need direct longitudinal and multi-institutional evidence. Generative AI should be treated as a supervised learning partner and an object of professional evaluation, not as an authoritative answer engine.

title: Industrial Engineering Design and Expertise in Improving the Efficiency of Work Systems
summary: Design is one of the core competencies in the field of Industrial Engineering, playing a crucial role in creating work systems that are effective, efficient, safe, high-quality, and cost-effective. Design focuses not only on product development but also encompasses the design of work systems, production processes, facility layouts, supply chains, organizational structures, and integrated information systems. In practice, an Industrial Engineering professional identifies a company’s needs, analyzes problems, and designs solutions based on scientific approaches and data analysis. Various methods used include work time analysis, productivity measurement, quality evaluation, ergonomics, cost optimization, and the utilization of digital technologies such as simulation, the Internet of Things (IoT), Artificial Intelligence (AI), and Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP). The application of appropriate design concepts can increase productivity, reduce waste, improve the quality of products and services, and enhance customer satisfaction. Thus, design capabilities are a strategic competency for Industrial Engineering graduates in supporting the improvement of organizational competitiveness in the era of digital transformation and the Fourth Industrial Revolution.

title: CLOUD-BASED ACCOUNTING TECHNOLOGY AND INNOVATIVE EFFICIENCY OF ACCOUNTING EDUCATORS AMONG UNIVERSITIES IN RIVERS AND BAYELSA STATES
summary: The study determines Cloud-based Accounting Technology and Innovative Efficiency of Accounting Educators in Universities in Rivers and Bayelsa States. The researchers adopted a correlational survey research design for the study. The study was carried out in the public universities in Rivers and Bayelsa States which includes. The population of this study consisted of 31 respondents, made up of Business Education (Accountancy) lecturers. The sample size of this study is 31 Accounting Education lecturers in public universities in Rivers and Bayelsa States, which is the entire population of the study; therefore, census enumeration was employed. The adoption of the entire population for the study is because the researchers considered manageable for the study. The instruments were subjected to face and content validation. The research instruments was validated by two Business Educators and an expert in Measurement and Evaluation. Cronbach alpha was used to test the internal consistency of the instruments and the reliability levels were established as coefficient index from the clusters; 0.73, 0.78, 0.81, 0.76, 0.89, 0.71 with an aggregate value of 0.78 which shows the sets of instruments are suitable and reliable for this study. The researchers personally administered the instrument to the respondents. Data collected were analysed using Pearson’s Product Moment Correlation (PPMC) to answer the three (3) research questions and used in testing the three (3) null hypotheses formulated, at 0.05 level of significance with the aid of statistical packages in social science (SPSS). Based on the findings, the following conclusions were made; that Sage, Quickbook and Freshbook have a positive relationship with innovative efficiency of Accounting Educators in Universities in Rivers and Bayelsa States. It was recommended among others; that university management should provide regular training for Accounting Educators in order to improve their innovative competencies on cloud-based accounting technology

title: Machine learning and big data in finance*
summary: Machine learning (ML) and the proliferation of large, granular, and unstructured data are reshaping how financial questions are posed and answered. Methods that relax the linearity, low dimensionality, and rigid distributional assumptions of classical econometrics are now applied across asset pricing, derivative valuation, forecasting, trading, risk management, and corporate finance. This special issue assembles nine contributions, which we organise around three themes: methodological advances in deep learning; ML for forecasting and dynamic decision-making; and explainable and applied ML in corporate finance and markets. Across the issue, common concerns emerge: interpretability, robustness across regimes, data quality, and the integration of economic structure with flexible learning. We introduce each contribution, situate it within the broader literature, and close by outlining open challenges and directions for future research.
